implemented_requirements.requirement: Two-player control with vertical paddles (up/down) for each player
implemented_requirements.evidence: Paddle.__init__ takes up_key and down_key; Paddle.update reads pygame.key.get_pressed() and moves the rect accordingly. Game creates left_paddle with KEY_LEFT_UP/KEY_LEFT_DOWN and right_paddle with KEY_RIGHT_UP/KEY_RIGHT_DOWN.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball bounces off top and bottom window edges
implemented_requirements.evidence: Ball.update checks self.rect.top <= 0 and self.rect.bottom >= settings.WINDOW_HEIGHT and reverses self.speed_y.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball bounces off paddles with angle variation
implemented_requirements.evidence: Ball.bounce_off_paddle computes offset from paddle centre, caps it, calculates angle = offset * BALL_MAX_BOUNCE_ANGLE and sets speed_x / speed_y accordingly.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Scoring when opponent misses the ball
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game._check_scoring increments score_left or score_right when ball.rect.right < 0 or ball.rect.left > WINDOW_WIDTH.
Game._check_scoring compares score_left / score_right against settings.WINNING_SCORE and switches to STATE_GAME_OVER.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Reset/serve ball after each point with a delay
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game._serve_ball calls ball.reset(direction) and sets serve_timer = SERVE_DELAY_MS; Game._update skips ball.update while serve_timer > 0.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game over overlay and ability to restart
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game._draw_game_over renders winner_text and prompt; Game._handle_events listens for KEY_RESTART to call _restart_match.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Main entry point that launches the game
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py defines main() which ensures pygame is installed, imports Game, creates an instance and calls run().

critical_issues: The automatic pygame installation in main.py may fail in environments without internet access or pip permissions, which could prevent execution.
No explicit handling for the case where the ball collides with a paddle while moving away (unlikely but possible due to high speed).
judge.summary: The provided source files contain a complete implementation of a two‑player Pong game meeting all core requirements: paddle control, ball physics with wall and paddle bounces, scoring, a configurable winning score, serve delays, and a restartable game‑over screen. The code is coherent and appears ready to run (assuming pygame can be installed). Minor concerns relate to dependency installation and an edge‑case collision scenario, but they do not affect the core functionality. Verdict: pass.
